clue.text: Drug provider causing fast internal damage

indicators.note: internal says one piece sits inside the other, here the damage within the fast word

parts.note: pacy means fast, quick on one's feet
to harm is to damage

explanation.surface: A chemist's shop is blamed for some rapid injury to a customer's insides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'internal' signals the container. 'Fast' looks like going without food, but here it means speedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist's shop dispenses medicines, so it is a supplier of drugs.

clue.text: It could be the end of written correspondence

definitions.text: It could be the end of written correspondence

parts.words: It could be the end of written correspondence
parts.note: read as a description of the extra note added below a letter's signature, written after the main text

explanation.definitionFit: An afterthought added at the foot of a letter, after the signature, is literally the last part of it.

clue.text: They take their leave without it

definitions.text: They take their leave without it

parts.words: They take their leave without it
parts.note: people who run off without permission, 'it' being the leave they were never granted

explanation.definitionFit: Fugitives who slip away secretly depart without being given any leave to go.

clue.text: Chief eastern state

parts.note: main means chief, principal

explanation.surface: The head of the eastern part of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is a US state in New England, in the far northeast.

clue.text: Brain transplant?

parts.note: swapping one thinking organ for another is pictured literally as a switch of thinking organ

explanation.definitionFit: Deciding differently is idiomatically a switch of opinion, here pictured as surgery swapping the organ itself.

clue.text: Jack lies about his descent

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB (able-bodied seaman) is a sailor too

indicators.note: about signals the word lies is turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Jack is lying about his ancestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LIES to SEIL. 'Jack' looks like a name; it is the sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope-controlled climb down a rock face is a type of descent.

clue.text: Gin from 1 across, used for a personal lift?

parts.note: Boots is a well-known British chain of chemist's shops, an example of the answer to 1 across
a gin is a trap for catching animals

explanation.surface: Gin bought at the chemist's to give oneself a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: Boots is a big British high-street chemist. 'Gin' is not the drink but a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling oneself up by one's own loops on a boot is the idiom for self-made improvement, a personal lift.

clue.text: Finishes despatch from first to last

indicators.note: says the opening letter is taken from the front and put at the end

parts.note: to despatch is to send off

explanation.surface: A message saying a delivery is complete, travelling all the way through.
explanation.definitionFit: Ends as a verb means finishes, both meaning comes to a close.

clue.text: Student and what one uses for joined-up writing?

definitions.text: Student and what one uses for joined-up writing?

parts.note: L is a learner, as on the L-plates of a student driver

parts.words: what one uses for joined-up writing
parts.note: ink is what one writes with

explanation.surface: A pupil and the pen-fluid needed for cursive handwriting.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a connection is what joins things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A connecting piece is something that joins things up, as the clue's hint at joining suggests.

clue.text: Verse form as in Tess, perhaps

definitions.note: singular in the clue while the answer is plural; read as instances of a verse form

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters may come in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A poetic form like the one used in Hardy's Tess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges AS IN TESS. Tess is a novel, not a poem, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Sestinas are poems of six six-line stanzas with repeated end words, a fixed verse form.

clue.text: Price, as in "One More River"

definitions.meaning: the spiritual 'One More River to Cross' refers to the river crossed into the Promised Land

explanation.definitionFit: The model Katie Price used this stage name, and the biblical river is the 'one more river' of the song.

clue.text: Talk of a time in Paul's experience

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: Saint Paul underwent a sudden religious conversion on the road to Damascus

explanation.surface: A discussion of an occasion in Paul's life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A and T inside CONVERSION.
explanation.definitionFit: A conversation is a talk between people.

clue.text: Hot stuff

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen, so hot stuff is loot rather than something sexy or spicy

explanation.definitionFit: Slang 'hot' means recently stolen, so hot stuff is property taken in a theft.

clue.text: Beverage buff serves teas in season

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the season

parts.note: winter is a season

indicators.note: serves suggests the word teas is dished out differently, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A drinks lover serves up tea during the cold months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serves' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container; 'Beverage' is wine, not the tea of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who samples and judges wines is an expert in one kind of drink.

clue.text: Battle, or prelude to a continual one?

definitions.meaning: a military ... is a fight between forces
a betrothal comes before marriage, jokingly pictured as a never-ending battle

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a military clash and the betrothal that precedes a marriage.

clue.text: Paces off street — maybe on horseback

indicators.note: off says the street abbreviation is taken away

parts.note: strides are long paces

explanation.surface: Someone walks off the road, perhaps on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who rides travels mounted, perhaps on a horse, or on a bike or bus.

clue.text: Americans who flout dietary regime?

parts.note: read as people who gobble (scoff) rules (laws), a play on the American term for habitual lawbreakers

explanation.definitionFit: An American word for people who habitually flout the law, split as eating plus rules.

clue.text: Translation of Obadiah turning up …

parts.note: Ob is the abbreviation for the biblical book of Obadiah
a version is a translation of a text

explanation.surface: A rendering of the Book of Obadiah appears.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to the next only in the surface. 'turning up' looks like 'appearing' but means turning to face.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the act of turning something so its face is shown, a technical sense of turning up.

clue.text: … according to ex-actor

parts.note: per means according to, as in 'per the rules'
ex means former, as in ex-wife

explanation.surface: Continuing: as told by a retired actor.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is one kind of performer, an entertainer on stage.

clue.text: Religious representation of classical characters

parts.note: pi is a Greek letter
eta is a Greek letter

explanation.surface: A religious image made of ancient figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classical characters' are letters of the Greek alphabet, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is a painting or sculpture of Mary holding the dead Christ, a religious image.

clue.text: Slave facing mutilation in the Hebrides

indicators.note: mutilation signals the letters are hacked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A slave about to be maimed in the Scottish islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mutilation' rearranges SLAVE FACING. The definition is a location, in the Hebrides, Scotland's western islands.
explanation.definitionFit: This sea cave on the isle of Staffa lies in the Inner Hebrides, so it is a feature found there.

clue.text: She puts up with a lot of harassment

indicators.note: puts up in a down clue says those letters are read upwards
a lot of says most of the word is taken, its first five letters

explanation.surface: A woman tolerates a great deal of bullying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' takes HARAS from harassment; 'puts up' turns it to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name stands for 'she', a female person.

clue.text: That is almost a fateful date

indicators.note: almost says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: id est is Latin for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Indeed, very nearly a doomed day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the T of ID EST, the Latin behind 'i.e.'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ides of March was the day Julius Caesar was assassinated, a famously fateful date.

clue.text: Old king of the soccer world

parts.note: taken as written
the FA, the Football Association, governs English soccer

explanation.surface: A veteran champion of football.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, famous for his dyke.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa ruled the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Mercia, an early English king.

clue.text: Government department unknown to pay out

parts.note: Defra is the UK Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An anonymous ministry handing over money.
explanation.walkthrough: DEFRA is the British environment ministry.
explanation.definitionFit: To defray costs is to pay them out, to settle expenses.

clue.text: Consumed minced tiger included in French savoury

indicators.note: included in places the chopped letters inside the other piece

parts.note: ate means consumed

indicators.note: minced says the word is chopped up into a new order

explanation.surface: A diner ate a French snack with minced tiger in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minced' is the anagram signal and 'included in' the container. An aigrette is also a heron's plume, but here it is the fritter.
explanation.definitionFit: An aigrette is a light cheese fritter, a French-style savoury dish.

clue.text: A press layout that's scanty

indicators.note: a layout is an arrangement, so the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: A newspaper page design with little on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly spread, meagre, the same as scanty.

clue.text: Solitary worker holds menial job

indicators.note: holds says one piece contains the other

parts.note: an ant is the classic worker insect
a chore is a menial task

explanation.surface: A lonely employee holds down a dull job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' signals the container. 'Solitary worker' reads as one phrase; the definition is only 'Solitary', a noun for a hermit.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchoret is a religious recluse, a solitary living apart from society.
